decision.summary: Full accepted IContract and the remaining ICampaignContractMarket are source-only facts carried on a journal-private field of ICampaignJournalEnvelope, a sibling of campaignEvent, never inside it. No grant scope -- campaign, team:, player:, or the GM all-scopes grant -- entitles a recipient to them over the wire, because no wire-bearing type names them.
decision.enforcingBoundary: envelopeOf (JournalCampaignEventStore.ts:177-181) returns stored.payload.campaignEvent and nothing else. CORRECTED 2026-09-15 after independent review: it is NOT the single narrowing today. It is used by JournalCampaignEventStore.ts:270 and :397, campaignJournalReads.ts:41 and :63, and GmCampaignImpactDerivation.ts:157, while grant projection narrows INLINE at projectCampaignStreamForGrant.ts:252 (const event = stored.payload.campaignEvent;) and never calls envelopeOf. The boundary is therefore two lines in two files today; task 6.1 carries an explicit obligation to route :252 through envelopeOf, collapsing it to one, and the spec SHALL is stated as an ADDED obligation rather than as current behavior.
decision.alternativeRejected: Explicit guest field projection -- classify each full-contract and market field, then add a redacting projector emitting a whitelisted subset to campaign-scope recipients.
rejectionGrounds: A second projection path would have to stay correct at three independent emission surfaces (grant projection, room-code recomposed hydration, client snapshot schema); a redactor any one surface bypasses leaks permanently because streams are immutable and reclassification is a new event, never an edit (D3).
It requires editing roomCodeGuestHydration.ts and a client schema, paths the recorded R2 implementation ceiling does not cover, so it would silently exceed the admitted prefix.
No product requirement names a guest-visible full-contract field; the compact projection already satisfies every current guest surface, so the whitelist would ship empty.

Under D3 the correct shape for a future guest-visible contract detail is a new event type stamped with its own scope carrying exactly that fact, not a field-level redactor over a payload whose default audience is already too wide.
decision.legacyBinding: The private field is conditionally constructed and absent when no admitted private payload exists; never an empty object and never an enumerable undefined property, because the canonicalizer rejects undefined and hashes exactly the enumerable own keys, and the state digest hashes the canonical state.
notAdmitted: any widening of the /commands response, guest hydration, or the co-op mirror
producer implementation, flag flip, or cutover; CAMPAIGN_JOURNAL_AUTHORITY_ENABLED remains false
authoritative materialization or replay of unrelated non-contract missions

resolutions.choice: ACCEPT as an explicit residual; do NOT exclude the private bytes from the digest material.
resolutions.justification: Excluding the private field from canonicalizeEventDigestV1 material would strip the private payload of the journal hash-chain tamper-evidence that D1 and D3 rest on -- the private facts would then be the only part of the envelope not covered by the chain, which is a worse property than a high-bar confirmation oracle. It would also require editing EventJournalCanonicalizer, shared by every stream type, a blast radius far outside this change and outside the cap. The carve-out is therefore stated positively (only the one-way commitment crosses; never the values), the private field is REQUIRED to stay inside the digest material, and a prohibition is added: the source exposes no surface confirming a candidate private payload against a delivered identity.
